subject: Next steps: GDPR contracting — DPA submission, SCC variant shortlist, and role alignment
messages:
From: Anna Weber <anna.weber@finpulse.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.example>
Cc: FinPulse Procurement <procure@finpulse.com>
Date: Sun, 29 Aug 2027 09:12:00 -0400
Subject: Follow-up on security items from today's demo

Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo earlier — that was really helpful. Procurement and legal asked me to follow up with a couple of concrete items so we can move the contracting thread along: 

1) Our DPA template (attached) — can you confirm whether Redwood will sign our DPA as-is or propose redlines? We need to get initial comments back to Legal by next Wednesday (2027-09-01).

2) SCCs — can you confirm which SCC module you prefer for FinPulse EU data (we currently expect Module 2 or the new Annex options)? If you have a recommended variant, please state it and the rationale.

3) Role mapping — we need explicit confirmation of controller vs. processor for the product flows we discussed (user-entered content + telemetry for performance). A short paragraph is fine.

4) SOC 2 — quick note: are you SOC 2 Type II ready? If not, what compensating controls or timelines should we note for procurement?

I attached our DPA for reference. Can you loop in the right folks on your side and share a short plan (who owns which deliverable + ETA)?

Best,
Anna
Anna Weber | Legal Operations
FinPulse

[attachment: finpulse_dpa_request_v1.pdf (application/pdf)]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.example>
To: Anna Weber <anna.weber@finpulse.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.example>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.example>
Date: Sun, 29 Aug 2027 11:08:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Follow-up on security items from today's demo

Hi Anna — great to meet you today, and thanks for the clear list. Quick responses below and a proposed next-steps plan.

Short answers up-front:
- DPA: we can start from your template. Legal will propose limited redlines around liability caps and data deletion timing; we'll return a marked copy by Tue 2027-08-31 EOD.
- SCCs: Redwood prefers the EU Commission standard clauses (Module 2 / processor-to-controller where applicable) for this use case. If FinPulse prefers the updated annex, we can support that, but legal prefers the classic wording for now — rationale: compatibility with our current vendor network and our private deployment options.
- Role mapping: Redwood acts as processor for FinPulse customer data (we process per your instructions); FinPulse is controller for user content collected from FinPulse users. We store customer logs in EU-hosted clusters when the customer selects EU region.
- SOC 2: Redwood is SOC 2 Type II in progress; latest Type II report completes in Q4 2027. For procurement, we can provide the Type I report and interim audit evidence (controls matrix + SOC readiness checklist) now.

Proposed next steps (owners + ETA):
- M: Upload our standard DPA draft and proposed redlines (attachment) — Marissa — 2027-08-31
- R: Confirm SCC module preference and prepare a 1-paragraph rationale for legal — Rishi — 2027-08-31
- L: Pull SOC documentation (Type I report, controls matrix) and share secure drive link — Laura — 2027-08-30
- A: Procurement to confirm whether the annex variant is required, or the classic SCCs will suffice — Anna/FinPulse — 2027-09-01

I'll attach our standard DPA for your review. Happy to jump on a 30-minute call if that speeds things up — Rishi and Laura are copied for legal/security details.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.example | +1 (415) 555-0128

[attachment: redwood_standard_dpa_v1.docx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document)]

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.example>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.example>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.example>
Date: Mon, 30 Aug 2027 08:22:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Follow-up on security items from today's demo

Marissa / Laura — quick internal note before we send final language to FinPulse: 

- SCC: Legal prefers Module 2 (processor-to-controller) for this engagement. The updated annex is acceptable only if procurement requires additional EU-specific wording; annex adds extra review time.
- Logs & data residency: confirm we will enforce EU-only storage for FinPulse when they select the EU region (no cross-border backups by default). If the customer requires geo-redundant backups in another region, that needs explicit clause in the DPA.
- SOC evidence: include the Type I report + current penetration test summary (redacted) and a controls matrix. If procurement flags SOC Type II as a gating item, propose a temporary attestation and an SLA credit / escrow clause.

I'll draft the short rationale and a proposed DPA redline for Marissa to send.

—Rishi
Rishi Malhotra | Head of Legal (Contracts) | Redwood Inference
rishi_malhotra@redwood.example
